title: Celcomen and causal disentanglement
takeaway: Celcomen is a 2026 spatial modeling framework intended to disentangle cell-intrinsic and microenvironmental contributions to expression.
explanation: A model tries to separate variation driven by own cell properties from environmental contributions.
caution: The word 'causal' in a model name does not independently validate interventions or identifiability assumptions.
question: What strengthens a claim of causal disentanglement?
options: Perturbation/identifiability tests and appropriate counterfactual validation
A UMAP with clear clusters
A high test-set correlation alone

reference.label: Megas et al., Celcomen, Nat Commun (2026), PMID 41851134

decisionRule: Separate explanatory correlates from causal effects: assess spatially matched controls, explicit assumptions and held-out perturbations before interpreting Celcomen parameters as intervention effects.

title: Intrinsic versus extrinsic expression signals
takeaway: A cell's measured RNA profile may reflect both its identity or internal state and signals arising from its microenvironment.
explanation: Two genetically similar cells in different niches may have different transcriptional responses.
caution: Associations cannot always cleanly separate environmental effects from intrinsic state without additional design.
question: Which is an extrinsic influence?
options: A secreted factor from a neighbor
A tumor cell's own DNA copy number
A stable inherited mutation only

reference.label: Megas et al., Celcomen, Nat Commun (2026), PMID 41851134

decisionRule: Ask whether the changed feature is intrinsic to a cell (genotype or internal state) or associated with neighborhood signals; compare matched cell types across different niches to test an extrinsic effect.

title: Spatial Perturb-Seq links perturbation and location
takeaway: Spatial Perturb-Seq combines molecular perturbation information with cell-expression and spatial measurements in intact tissue.
explanation: An in vivo barcoded CRISPR perturbation in mouse brain is read out with spatial transcriptomic platforms.
caution: The 2026 experimental validation described mouse brain; do not generalize to human GBM without new data.
question: Which observation is more causal than mere co-localization?
options: A controlled perturbation and spatially resolved downstream readout
Two cells expressing complementary ligands
A colorful neighborhood plot

reference.label: Shen et al., Spatial Perturb-Seq, Nat Commun (2026)

decisionRule: A spatial perturbation assay needs an identified intervention per cell or clone, spatial readout and suitable controls. Co-localization without perturbation supports association only.

title: NK cells vs cytotoxic CD8 T cells: what actually distinguishes them?
takeaway: Cytotoxicity genes do not identify lineage. Use a coherent T-cell receptor/CD3 program (CD3D, CD3E, CD3G, TRAC/TRBC1/2) together with CD8A/CD8B to support CD8 T identity; a conventional NK population has an NK-receptor program without a conventional TCR. A single absent transcript is not proof.
explanation: NKG7, GNLY, PRF1 and GZMB are effector-program genes shared by NK and cytotoxic T cells. In contrast, a coherent CD3/TCR program, especially TRAC and TRBC with CD3 genes, supports αβ T-cell lineage. CD8A/CD8B further supports a CD8 T-cell phenotype. Conventional NK cells are often enriched for KLRD1 (CD94), NCR1 (NKp46), NCAM1 (CD56), FCGR3A (CD16), KLRC1, TYROBP or FCER1G, but expression varies by subtype and some are not exclusive to NK. Importantly, cytotoxic glioma-infiltrating CD8 T cells can express KLRD1, KLRB1 and other NK receptors. Prioritize T-cell receptor evidence over a single NK-associated marker.
caution: NKG7, GNLY, GZMB, PRF1, KLRD1, CD161/KLRB1 and CD56 are not individually decisive. Sparse RNA assays can miss CD3/TCR transcripts. FCGR3A can also be expressed by myeloid cells. Co-occurring TCR and NK signatures can reflect NK-like T cells, NKT cells, doublets or contamination; check coordinated markers and, where possible, TCR sequencing plus CD3/CD8/CD56 protein. This is for human data; mouse markers require separate evaluation.
question: Two human GBM cytotoxic lymphocytes both express NKG7 and KLRD1. Cell A: CD3E+, TRAC+, CD8B+. Cell B: NCAM1+, NCR1+, FCER1G+, with no detected TCR transcripts. Which interpretation is best supported?
options: A is a cytotoxic CD8 T cell with an NK-associated program; B is an NK candidate that needs confirmation
Both are NK cells because KLRD1 is expressed in each
A must be an NKT cell, while B is definitively conventional NK based on absent TCR reads

reference.label: Mathewson et al., Cell (2021), PMID 33592174, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2021.01.022

decisionRule: First ask whether there is a coherent αβ TCR/CD3 signal (TRAC, TRBC1/2, CD3D/E/G). If yes, and CD8A/CD8B are present, favor CD8 T-cell lineage even when KLRD1/GNLY are high. If conventional TCR/CD3 evidence is repeatedly absent but multiple NK-associated receptors are coherent, consider NK. With only NKG7/GNLY or a few zero counts, retain an ambiguous cytotoxic lymphocyte label.

contrast.right: No coherent conventional αβ TCR program

contrast.left: CD8A, CD8B, TCR clonotype when available
contrast.right: KLRD1, NCR1, NCAM1, KLRC1; FCGR3A in some NK subsets

contrast.left: Surface CD3+ CD8+, productive αβ TCR
contrast.right: Surface CD3− CD56+ and/or CD16+ with coherent NK phenotype

workedExamples.profile: CD3D+, CD3E+, TRAC+, CD8A+, CD8B+, NKG7+, KLRD1+
workedExamples.answer: Cytotoxic CD8 T cell with an NK-like receptor program
workedExamples.why: The coherent TCR/CD3 signature outweighs KLRD1, which is also reported in glioma-infiltrating CD8 T cells.

workedExamples.profile: CD3/TCR not detected, KLRD1+, NCR1+, NCAM1+, NKG7+, FCGR3A+
workedExamples.why: A coherent NK program and no conventional TCR evidence support NK, but low-depth RNA counts cannot prove TCR absence.

workedExamples.profile: NKG7+, GNLY+, GZMB+; CD3/TCR and NK receptors mostly undetected
workedExamples.why: Shared effector genes alone cannot distinguish lineage.

optionFeedback: Correct: A has coherent TCR/CD8 lineage evidence despite KLRD1. B has a coordinated NK-associated pattern, but nondetection of TCR can reflect RNA dropout and needs orthogonal validation.
Incorrect: KLRD1 is also expressed by glioma-infiltrating CD8 T cells; it cannot override a coherent CD3/TCR signature.
Incorrect: an NK-like cytotoxic program does not prove invariant NKT identity in A, and sparse negative TCR reads do not definitively establish NK identity in B.

title: Giotto is a spatial-analysis toolbox
takeaway: Giotto implements methods for characterizing tissue composition, spatial expression patterns and cellular interactions.
explanation: A researcher can analyze and visualize spatial transcriptomic or proteomic tissue data.
caution: Its inferred interactions are computational associations rather than automatically demonstrated signaling.
question: What task is explicitly in Giotto's scope?
options: Spatial expression and cell-neighborhood analyses
Measuring DNA mutations without sequencing
Performing clinical irradiation

reference.label: Dries et al., Giotto, Genome Biol (2021), PMID 33685491

decisionRule: Use Giotto to measure spatial enrichment, domain boundaries or ligand–receptor *co-occurrence*; confirm signaling separately with protein or perturbation evidence.

title: Tissues are multicellular systems
takeaway: Many tissues contain multiple cell types whose collective organization contributes to function.
explanation: A tissue section includes diverse cellular compartments and extracellular structures.
caution: Cell-type proportions alone do not fully characterize multicellular function.
question: What is lost when only cell-type counts are retained?
options: Spatial organization and some functional context
The existence of cell types
The measured sample identity

reference.label: Dries et al., Giotto, Genome Biol (2021), PMID 33685491

decisionRule: Two tissues may have identical cell-type proportions but different adjacency graphs. Examine cell–cell neighborhoods and spatial organization instead of counts alone.

title: ResolVI follows segmentation
takeaway: ResolVI is a probabilistic correction model applied to initial expression counts and spatial positions produced by an upstream quantification/segmentation pipeline.
explanation: A segmentation algorithm assigns molecules to cells; ResolVI models expression affected by misassignment and nuisance variation.
caution: ResolVI does not segment raw microscopy images de novo and depends on the quality of initial cell estimates.
question: A Xenium dataset has molecules assigned to segmented cells. You want ResolVI to correct contamination. Which pipeline is appropriate?
options: Run segmentation and initial quantification first, then model cell expression and misassignment with ResolVI
Run ResolVI directly on raw pixel intensities and get cell boundaries
Use ResolVI to infer chromosomal copy number from DNA-only imaging

reference.label: Ergen & Yosef, ResolVI, Nat Methods (2026)

decisionRule: Check the input: ResolVI follows a segmentation/molecule-assignment pipeline and takes quantified cell-by-gene observations with spatial context. It cannot replace segmentation of raw images.
optionFeedback: Correct: ResolVI models cell-level spatial transcript counts downstream of segmentation and quantification.
Incorrect: the method is not a raw-image cell segmentation algorithm.
Incorrect: the intended inference is expression/misassignment, not DNA chromosome counting.

title: Spurious RNA mixing has multiple causes
takeaway: Apparent RNA in one cell may include molecules misassigned from neighbors through segmentation, tissue leakage or three-dimensional overlap.
explanation: A neuron-associated transcript may be falsely counted in a nearby microglial segment.
caution: A correction model's outputs are estimated, not direct ground-truth molecular ownership.
question: A segment annotated as microglia contains a few neuronal transcripts near a large neurite. What is the strongest first interpretation?
options: Test geometry, RNA spillover and assignment errors before asserting a biological hybrid state
Confirm conversion from a neuron to microglia from one shared marker
Discard microglial identity because one neuronal transcript is present

reference.label: Ergen & Yosef, ResolVI, Nat Methods (2026)

decisionRule: Audit marker molecules against cellular boundaries, 3D overlap, local diffusion and negatives. A surprising mixed transcript signal can be technical before biological.
optionFeedback: Correct: molecules can be misassigned because cells and processes overlap in 3D, especially in spatial imaging.
Incorrect: genuine transdifferentiation needs substantially stronger independent evidence.
Incorrect: low-level mixed transcripts can occur even when the cell-type assignment is otherwise plausible.

title: Spatial RNA platforms have distinct readouts
takeaway: High-resolution spatial assays may capture barcoded RNA for sequencing or visualize individual labeled RNA molecules by imaging.
explanation: Sequencing-based spots and imaging-based molecular coordinates yield different error models.
caution: The spot-based versus imaging-based distinction is broad; platforms vary in chemistry, panel breadth and resolution.
question: What differentiates imaging-based molecule-resolved assays?
options: Individual probe-labeled RNA molecules are localized optically
They always sequence intact whole genomes
They necessarily have no segmentation errors

reference.label: Ergen & Yosef, ResolVI, Nat Methods (2026)

decisionRule: Identify measurement modality: barcoded spatial sequencing gives regional RNA counts, while imaging locates probe-labeled molecules; read length, panel and cell-assignment constraints differ.

title: Nicheformer jointly pretrains on dissociated and spatial cells
takeaway: Nicheformer is a transformer-based foundation model trained across spatial and dissociated single-cell datasets.
explanation: A shared representation can transfer some information about local tissue contexts.
caution: An embedding is a learned prediction tool; it is not direct observation of hidden cell neighborhoods.
question: What is distinctive about Nicheformer's pretraining?
options: It includes spatial and dissociated single-cell data
It is trained only on bulk histology
It requires patient-specific radiation labels

reference.label: Tejada-Lapuerta et al., Nicheformer, Nat Methods (2025)

decisionRule: Nicheformer leverages both spatial and dissociated transcriptomic corpora with technology/species context. Learned representations do not re-create known true coordinates for dissociated cells.

title: Single-cell transformers need more than architecture names
takeaway: Foundation models such as scGPT, Geneformer and Nicheformer employ learned cell representations but differ in tokenization and objectives.
explanation: A model can tokenize gene identities, expression ranks and contextual variables differently.
caution: Shared attention architecture does not guarantee transferable biological mechanisms.
question: What must be compared to assess two cell foundation models?
options: Tokenization, training data, objectives and evaluation
Only the word 'transformer' in the title
Only the number of layers

reference.label: Tejada-Lapuerta et al., Nicheformer, Nat Methods (2025)

decisionRule: Compare input/tokenization and pretraining loss rather than model names: Geneformer uses rank-encoded genes; scGPT and Nicheformer use different expression and context encodings.

title: Dissociated profiling loses coordinates
takeaway: Conventional dissociated scRNA-seq offers cell-resolved expression but discards original within-tissue cell coordinates.
explanation: Spatial transcriptomics retains location, with technology-dependent resolution.
caution: A cell's original niche cannot be uniquely reconstructed from its dissociated expression alone.
question: What is the central information loss of standard scRNA-seq dissociation?
options: Original tissue-neighborhood coordinates
RNA counts per captured cell
Ability to identify genes

reference.label: Tejada-Lapuerta et al., Nicheformer, Nat Methods (2025)

decisionRule: Ask whether spatial coordinates were measured before dissociation. Without them, any reconstructed neighborhood is inferred, not directly observed.

title: Scale does not establish biological generalization
takeaway: Nicheformer was pretrained on SpatialCorpus-110M, combining over 57 million dissociated and 53 million spatially resolved cells.
explanation: Large multi-tissue corpora permit broad representation learning.
caution: Dataset size is not a substitute for out-of-distribution evaluation or causal tests.
question: What does 110M describe for Nicheformer?
options: Approximate total cells in its curated pretraining corpus
110 million genes in each cell
Number of patient interventions

reference.label: Tejada-Lapuerta et al., Nicheformer, Nat Methods (2025)

decisionRule: Inspect held-out technology, tissue and donor evaluation after pretraining. A 110-million-cell corpus alone does not establish accurate GBM transfer.

title: DNA-anchored malignant classification
takeaway: DNA-level alterations can provide stronger direct evidence of cancer lineage than expression-based CNV inference.
explanation: Tumor cells with somatic changes can be distinguished from nonmalignant populations.
caution: Not every cancer cell carries every selected marker; DNA evidence quality and clonal heterogeneity matter.
question: Which is most direct for detecting a chromosome gain?
options: A calibrated DNA copy-number assay
One overexpressed gene
A cell's spatial coordinates

reference.label: GBM spatial atlas, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: For malignant status or chromosome gains, prefer a variant- or copy-number assay that directly measures DNA; use RNA-derived CNVs as a screening hypothesis.

title: Targeted FFPE probes are panel-limited
takeaway: Probe-based spatial RNA assays detect preselected transcript targets in preserved tissue, including FFPE-compatible workflows.
explanation: A targeted panel can map selected genes with high spatial resolution.
caution: No probe for a transcript means it will not be directly quantified; assay processing and segmentation affect results.
question: Can a targeted 500-gene panel directly measure every transcriptome gene?
options: No, only its measured targets
Yes, every unmeasured gene becomes ground truth
Yes, RNA velocity is automatic

reference.label: Ergen & Yosef, ResolVI, Nat Methods (2026)

decisionRule: An FFPE assay with a fixed probe panel reports only targeted transcripts. Missing gene measurements must be labeled unobserved or imputed, not treated as zeros or ground truth.

title: Visium spots versus molecule-level imaging
takeaway: Classic Visium aggregates expression over spots that can contain multiple cells; Xenium, CosMx and MERFISH locate targeted individual RNA molecules.
explanation: A cell-segmentation step can assign imaged molecules to cellular regions.
caution: Molecule-level imaging still has panel, detection, assignment and 3D-overlap limitations.
question: Visium and Xenium profile adjacent GBM sections. Which is a correct statement about what they directly observe?
options: Classic Visium gives mixed spot expression; Xenium localizes targeted RNA molecules before cell assignment
Both provide exact full-transcriptome counts for every cell
Visium directly records each RNA molecule's 3D source cell and Xenium never needs segmentation

reference.label: Ståhl et al., spatial transcriptomics, Science (2016)

decisionRule: Classic Visium measures mixed multicellular spots, whereas Xenium/CosMx/MERFISH image individual targeted transcripts and depend on segmentation to get cell-level counts.
optionFeedback: Correct: the direct observation is a spot-count matrix versus imaged probe-based molecule coordinates.
Incorrect: imaging spatial assays are panel-limited and classic Visium spots may include multiple cells.
Incorrect: the two assays have different resolution and assignment constraints; neither guarantees perfect cell ownership.

title: An absolute GBM intron claim is not established
takeaway: The saved statement that no sub-100-µm human GBM dataset observes introns is too broad to accept without a systematic platform- and dataset-level audit.
explanation: Whether spliced/unspliced counts are usable depends on chemistry, assay processing, raw data access and annotation.
caution: Could not verify with peer-reviewed sources that RNA velocity at cell resolution is categorically impossible for all GBM spatial data.
question: What would be required to rule out a specific velocity analysis?
options: Inspect raw chemistry/read structure and intron quantifiability for the dataset
Infer absence from spot diameter alone
Assume all imaging platforms measure full transcriptomes

reference.label: La Manno et al., RNA velocity, Nature (2018)

decisionRule: For RNA velocity, inspect BAM/read structure for intronic coverage and compute usable gene-specific spliced/unspliced counts; 2D resolution alone is not an impossibility proof.

title: Sparse autoencoders are not a new 2026 invention
takeaway: Sparse coding and sparsity-regularized autoencoders predate the modern use of SAEs to interpret transformer representations.
explanation: SAEs encourage relatively sparse feature activations that can sometimes be interpretable.
caution: The exact historical attribution in the note was not systematically verified; a particular variant's novelty needs precise citation.
question: What makes an autoencoder 'sparse' in this context?
options: An objective/constraint encouraging limited feature activation
Its encoder must have zero weights
Every latent feature must represent one gene

reference.label: Kendiukhov, J Biomed Inform (2026), PMID 42155660

decisionRule: Check the sparsity constraint (for example L1 or top-k), reconstruction error and stability across random seeds. A sparse latent factor is not automatically a regulatory mechanism.

title: Cell type and cell state are different analytical levels
takeaway: Cell type captures a relatively persistent identity, while state captures context-dependent activity or condition.
explanation: A microglial cell retains lineage identity while adopting an activated inflammatory state.
caution: Type/state separation is an analytical abstraction, and plasticity can blur some categories.
question: A malignant GBM cell expresses astrocytic markers, while a nearby normal astrocyte activates injury-response genes. Which labels are supported?
options: Malignant cell: AC-like transcriptional state; normal astrocyte: reactive state, if independently identified
Both cells must be normal astrocytes
Both cells must be malignant AC-like cells

reference.label: GBM spatial atlas, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Within the same microglial lineage, activated versus resting signatures indicate cell states; neuron versus microglia refers to cell types. Malignant mimics require extra identification.
optionFeedback: Correct: type/lineage and transient expression state are different axes; malignant identity must be separately validated.
Incorrect: a tumor cell can resemble a normal astrocyte transcriptomically without becoming normal.
Incorrect: injury-response marker expression alone cannot prove an astrocyte is malignant.

title: GENCODE is genome annotation
takeaway: GENCODE provides reference gene and transcript annotation, including coordinates, exon structure and transcript identifiers.
explanation: An RNA-seq pipeline uses transcript annotation when assigning reads.
caution: Annotations are version- and genome-build-dependent, and they do not by themselves establish true expression.
question: What does GENCODE supply?
options: Gene/transcript coordinates and exon annotations
Measured protein abundance in a sample
Patient-specific radiation dose

reference.label: Stuart & Satija, Nat Rev Genet (2019)

decisionRule: Confirm genome build (for example GRCh38) and GENCODE version before interpreting exon junctions or transcript coordinates; annotation does not measure expression.

title: Multimodal single-cell measurements
takeaway: Single-cell multi-omics assays or integrations combine RNA with other measurements such as chromatin accessibility or proteins.
explanation: Paired modalities can characterize a cell more richly than RNA alone.
caution: Not every 'multimodal' paper assays all modalities in the same cells; paired versus integrated data differ.
question: A study integrates scRNA-seq from donor A and scATAC-seq from donor B and calls the result 'multimodal'. What must you verify before claiming cell-level RNA–ATAC concordance?
options: Whether both modalities were measured in the very same indexed cells or computationally aligned across samples
Whether the two UMAPs have similar axis names
Whether both assays used the same gene symbols

reference.label: Stuart & Satija, Nat Rev Genet (2019)

decisionRule: Paired multiome assays measure different modalities in the same indexed nucleus; separate scRNA and scATAC cohorts merely integrated computationally are not same-cell ground truth.
optionFeedback: Correct: multi-omics measured in the same cell is different from computational cross-assay integration.
Incorrect: matching visualization axes does not establish matching biological cells.
Incorrect: shared gene symbols allow mapping but not evidence of paired cell-level observation.

title: A preprint is not the same as peer-reviewed validation
takeaway: A 2026 arXiv note proposes Top-K SAE analyses across scGPT and Geneformer representations.
explanation: Preprints can motivate replication or competitive-method searches.
caution: The specific arXiv claim has not been independently checked as peer reviewed; its findings must be labeled provisional.
question: What evidence is needed before calling a preprint peer reviewed?
options: Publication and review status of the exact version
A large model parameter count
A citation in a chat response

reference.label: Kendiukhov, J Biomed Inform (2026), PMID 42155660

decisionRule: Find a peer-reviewed journal publication for the exact claims/figures, not just an arXiv identifier; version and publication date matter.

title: SAEs on scGPT already have peer-reviewed precedent
takeaway: Kendiukhov (2026, Journal of Biomedical Informatics) examined sparse autoencoders for interpreting single-cell foundation-model representations.
explanation: A new SAE-for-scGPT project should compare against prior interpretable-feature analyses.
caution: Peer review of the underlying study does not mean any future SAE result is biologically causal.
question: What does this publication affect most directly?
options: The novelty claim of a generic SAE-on-scGPT cell-type project
The number of chromosomes in GBM
Whether RNA is double stranded

reference.label: Kendiukhov, J Biomed Inform (2026), PMID 42155660

decisionRule: Compare a new SAE–scGPT feature-analysis proposal with Kendiukhov's peer-reviewed 2026 methodology and evaluations before claiming novelty.

title: AT1 and AT2 are lung epithelial cell types
takeaway: Alveolar type 1 (AT1) and type 2 (AT2) cells are different alveolar epithelial populations.
explanation: AT2 cells synthesize pulmonary surfactant; AT1 cells contribute to the thin gas-exchange interface.
caution: Their markers and differentiation relationships are context-dependent; they are not brain glia.
question: Human lung scRNA-seq: one epithelial population has high SFTPC/SFTPB, another AGER-associated signatures. Which interpretation is most supported?
options: First is AT2-like surfactant-producing epithelium; second is AT1-like gas-exchange epithelium
First is AT1 because surfactant synthesis defines AT1
Both are endothelial cells because they reside in alveoli

reference.label: Stuart & Satija, Nat Rev Genet (2019)

decisionRule: Human AT1 cells are generally associated with gas-exchange membrane programs (such as AGER), while AT2 cells with surfactant genes (such as SFTPC); use a panel, not one marker alone.
optionFeedback: Correct: surfactant protein gene programs are typical of AT2, whereas AGER is associated with human AT1 cells.
Incorrect: AT2 cells are the major pulmonary surfactant-producing alveolar epithelial cells.
Incorrect: alveolar epithelial cells are not defined as vascular endothelium by their anatomical location.

title: Solo detects potential doublets
takeaway: Solo uses a VAE representation of single-cell RNA data and a classifier trained with simulated doublets.
explanation: An observed droplet containing two cells may be classified by comparison with artificial doublets.
caution: Solo estimates doublet likelihood; classifications are not perfect proof of one or two real captured cells.
question: What training contrast does Solo exploit?
options: Simulated doublets versus observed cells
Histology labels versus protein arrays
Tumor DNA versus blood oxygen

reference.label: Bernstein et al., Solo, Cell Syst (2020), PMID 32592658

decisionRule: Solo generates artificial doublets from observed profiles and trains a discriminator on learned scVI representations. Predicted doublet probability is a model score, not a counted second cell.

title: AE versus VAE
takeaway: An autoencoder learns a deterministic representation and reconstruction; a variational autoencoder fits a probabilistic latent-variable model with regularization.
explanation: VAEs use an approximate posterior and a generative likelihood, whereas a basic AE minimizes reconstruction loss.
caution: Both families have many architectures; an AE is not necessarily linear and a VAE is not guaranteed to model biological causation.
question: An AE and a VAE both reconstruct the same scRNA-seq matrix. Which observation most directly distinguishes the VAE objective?
options: An approximate posterior q(z|x), a prior p(z) and a KL-divergence term in the loss
Low-dimensional latent embeddings, which only VAEs can produce
A decoder network, which standard AEs do not contain

reference.label: Stuart & Satija, Nat Rev Genet (2019)

decisionRule: AE: encode a point z and reconstruct x. VAE: infer a distribution q(z|x), sample z, optimize reconstruction plus a KL regularizer against a prior. Both can be nonlinear.
optionFeedback: Correct: the probabilistic latent-variable formulation and ELBO-style objective distinguish the standard VAE from a plain AE.
Incorrect: both autoencoders and variational autoencoders learn latent representations.
Incorrect: both families normally include a decoder.

title: Linear autoencoders and PCA
takeaway: Under specific objectives and constraints, a linear autoencoder can recover the principal subspace of PCA.
explanation: SVD finds orthogonal principal components that explain variance of centered data.
caution: Not every linear autoencoder returns the unique PCA loadings or uses the transpose of its encoder matrix.
question: A centered expression matrix is analyzed with PCA and a linear AE with squared reconstruction error. Their latent subspaces match, but weights differ. Is this surprising?
options: No; the linear AE can recover the PCA subspace without returning the same uniquely oriented loadings
Yes; all learned AE weights must exactly equal PCA eigenvectors
No; PCA always uses a nonlinear objective unrelated to reconstruction

reference.label: Linear autoencoders and PCA — scientific reference search

decisionRule: PCA is a linear orthogonal variance-maximizing subspace (with centering); a linear AE can span that subspace under appropriate loss and constraints, but its raw weights need not equal PCA loadings.
optionFeedback: Correct: matching subspaces does not require matching coordinates or raw encoder weights.
Incorrect: linear AE weight matrices can differ under basis transformations and parameterization.
Incorrect: PCA is a linear subspace method that can be framed through reconstruction error.
